transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because I can’t seem to sit still when I’m supposed to. It feels like there’s a motor running under my skin, especially in staff meetings or briefings at church. I’ll start shifting around, standing up, or finding some reason to get up and move. It’s been bothering me enough that I figured I should talk to someone.
Did you experience these feelings of restlessness when you were a child?

Yes, I did. I remember in grade school getting in trouble for popping out of my seat and talking over the teacher. I’d also rush ahead before the directions were even finished. My mother used to say I acted like I was wound too tight, even back then.
Did you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they finished speaking when you were a child?

Yes, I did. I’d blurt things out before the teacher or whoever was talking finished. Even now I catch myself doing it—like if my supervisor or someone at church is giving instructions, I’ll jump in with what I think they’re about to say, and sometimes I’m wrong and they have to correct me.
Did you often get into physical fights or engage in risky behaviors as a child?

I don’t really remember that being a big thing. I wasn’t getting into fights all the time or doing dangerous stuff, at least not that I can clearly point to. My trouble was more with being restless and speaking before thinking.
Did you often have difficulty paying attention to details or making careless mistakes in your work or activities as a child?
I’m not really sure about that one. I don’t remember being told I made a lot of careless mistakes or missed details as a kid. That wasn’t something that stands out to me.
Do you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they finished speaking in your current daily life?

Yes, I still do that. Like when my supervisor or someone from the church staff is giving me instructions, I’ll jump in with what I think they’re about to say before they finish. Sometimes I’m wrong, and then they have to stop and correct me.
Do you often act on impulse in your daily life, doing things without fully thinking them through?

Yes, I guess I do in that way. Like with instructions, I’ll jump in before the person is done talking because I think I already know where they’re going. Then sometimes I’m wrong, and my supervisor or someone at the church has to stop and correct me.
Do you often have difficulty paying attention to details or making careless mistakes in your work or daily activities now?
I’m not sure I’d say that’s a big issue for me now. I don’t really notice making a lot of careless mistakes or missing details in my work. If it happens, it’s not something that stands out to me.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks and activities in your daily life?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed that as a major problem day to day. I usually just do what needs to be done, but I don’t know if I’d call it trouble organizing.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things around you?
I don’t really know. I can get sidetracked sometimes, sure, but I haven’t noticed it being a constant thing where everything around me pulls my attention away.
Do you often have trouble sustaining focus during tasks?
I’m not sure. I can usually stay with a task if I know what I’m doing, especially at work. I might drift a little sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed a big problem with keeping focus.
Do you often struggle to follow through on instructions or finish tasks at work or in other activities?

I’m not sure I’d say that happens often. If someone gives me instructions, I usually try to get it done. I might need to double-check what they wanted sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed a big problem with not finishing tasks.
Do you often have difficulty keeping your workspace or living space organized?

I don’t think that’s a big issue for me. I mean, things can get a little messy sometimes, but I usually know where things are and I clean up when I need to. I haven’t really noticed it causing problems.
Do you often feel excessively fidgety or restless when you're sitting still, like in meetings or other quiet situations?

Yes, that’s actually one of the main things bothering me. When I’m supposed to sit still, like in staff meetings or even church briefings, I feel like there’s a motor running under my skin. I start shifting around, or I’ll stand up, or I’ll look for some reason to move around. It’s hard for me to just sit there quietly.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety at home or when you're relaxing?

Yeah, I do. Even at home or when I’m supposed to be relaxing, I have a hard time just sitting still and being quiet. Like if I’m fishing with my wife, I’ll be tapping or messing with my tackle box instead of just waiting. Or at bingo, I’ll catch myself talking too loud or fiddling with the pencil. It’s like I can’t quite settle down and just enjoy it.
Do you feel like your restlessness and impulsive behaviors are causing problems in your relationships or at work?

Yes, mostly at work. It’s started causing some problems there. I’ll miss part of what someone told me to do, or I’ll jump into decisions about supplies or room turnovers too fast, and then it creates friction with coworkers. My supervisor has had to correct me a few times, and he actually suggested I go through the employee assistance program. So, yeah, it’s affecting things more than I’d like to admit.
Have you experienced these symptoms of restlessness and impulsivity consistently throughout your adult life?

Not really throughout my whole adult life, no. I mean, I’ve probably always been a bit restless, but this worse stretch has been going on about a year and five months. It started after my cleaning contract changed to rotating hours and more event work.
Have you ever been diagnosed with any other mental health conditions?
No, not that I know of. I haven’t really been diagnosed with anything else mental health-wise.
Do you often forget things you were supposed to do, like appointments or tasks?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I don’t think I forget appointments all that often. With tasks, maybe here and there, but I haven’t really been keeping track of it.
Have your symptoms of restlessness and impulsivity been present for at least 6 months?
Yes, definitely more than 6 months. It’s been about a year and five months now, since my cleaning contract switched to rotating hours and more event work.
